![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226903/assets/9bb15934c271a17851342b9032f5096f48e7ac9ee4e149af92ac1010dea46d88.png)

Calculate the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)=3xy\,i+(2x+1)\,j$ through the curve $C$ given by $r(t)=t\,i+t\,j$ for $t\in [0,1],$ measured with respect to the unit normal vector $n$ on $C,$ as shown above.
question.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple curve, then the flux of $F$ across $C$ measured with respect to a unit normal vector $n$ on $C$ is given by

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={\int }_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x.
$$

To apply this formula, 

- the curve should be parameterized as $r(t)$ for $t\in [a,b],$ and

- the unit normal vector $n$ *must* be a ${90}^{∘}$ clockwise rotation of the unit tangent vector $T(t).$

In this case, $n$ is indeed a ${90}^{∘}$ clockwise rotation of $T,$ so we can apply the above formula. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226903/assets/0e751adb9f44d24ba89af318fe5f063b1be146bbae45d05fc2dd9a99bef259f2.png)

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=t,\,y=t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x,y) & =3xy=3{t}^{2}, \\ Q(x,y) & =2x+1=2t+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ along the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)=1, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(P\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-Q\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(3{t}^{2})(1)-(2t+1)(1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3{t}^{2}-2t-1\,\text{d}t \\  & =({t}^{3}-{t}^{2}-t){|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(1-1-1)-(0-0-0) \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$
